---
title: "How the overview is built"
description: "Where the workflow graphs README lives, which text is yours, where outcomes come from, and what can't be shown."
---

Background to the [workflow graphs](workflow-graphs.qmd): what is
generated, what you can adjust, and the limits of what can be read from
workflow files.

## Why a folder of its own

The overview lives in `.github/workflow-graphs/README.md`, not inside
`.github/workflows/`. GitHub treats every file in `.github/workflows/` as
a workflow file, and a GitHub App may only change those with an extra
*Workflows* permission — which would also let it change your actual
workflows. A folder of its own needs no such permission. And never
`.github/README.md`: GitHub would show that one instead of your
repository's front page.

## Your own text is kept

The table and diagrams sit between two marker comments,
`<!-- workflow-graphs:overview:start -->` and `…:end -->`. Only that
block is ever replaced. The first run writes a short introduction around
it; after that, everything outside the block is yours — add explanations
above or below it, rewrite the introduction.

## What workflows produce

What a workflow produces can't be read from its YAML reliably, so it is
described in `config/workflow-outcomes.yml` of this repository — for all
workflows here. Workflows that aren't listed simply get no outcome boxes.
To describe your own workflows, put a copy of that file at the same path
in your repository ([as for the other settings](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance))
and add them, e.g. `.github/workflows/deploy.yml: [commit]` or your own
wording, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml: ["Site deployed to {environment}"]`
— `{environment}` is filled in from the calling job's input of that name.
Conditions under which a job runs are added automatically. A result that
depends on the event is written as
`{outcome: commit, only-on: push}`.

## Chains between workflows

To find where one workflow starts another, the called reusable workflows
are read too, at the version you reference. Found are `workflow_run`
triggers, and dispatches sent with `gh api …/dispatches`,
`gh workflow run` or the common dispatch actions. A dispatch sent in
another way — or from inside a composite action — shows no arrow. A
called workflow in a private repository the job can't read is still shown,
marked "not readable".

## What can't be shown

Links that exist only through repository settings don't appear — for
example a branch rule that requires a check to pass before a pull request
can be merged. The overview shows what the workflow files say.
